title: Trust:
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Safety first: a trusted adult and Childline Kenya 116. Do not role-play touching.

skills.key_step: The child retells Genesis 39:7-12: Potiphar's wife tempts Joseph, he refuses because it would be a sin against God, he keeps away and runs out leaving his cloak; God sees even when no one else does.

floor.prerequisite: Knows Joseph later explained Pharaoh's dreams.
floor.question: Whose dreams did Joseph explain?

representations: a door and a cloak left behind
steps: Joseph is a servant in Potiphar's house.
He is tempted day after day.
He says it is a sin against God.
He runs out, leaving his cloak.
contexts: being dared to watch a bad video
a friend pressing you to cheat
an older person asking you to keep a wrong secret

board.do: Draw a doorway and a cloak on the floor.

board.say: Why did Joseph leave his cloak behind?

board.do: Wait for the child to say he ran from sin.

listen_for: He was afraid of his master
misconceptions.ask: Why did Joseph refuse, according to Genesis 39:9?
What did Joseph do when she held on to his cloak?

listen_for: No one is here, so no one will know
misconceptions.ask: Joseph was alone with her in the house. What was his reasoning?

listen_for: He was made a ruler at once
misconceptions.ask: What happened to Joseph soon after he refused Potiphar's wife?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 39:20 and then 41:41: doing right was costly first; God was with him in prison.

checks.question: Why did Joseph refuse, according to Genesis 39:9?
checks.answer: It would be a sin against God

checks.question: What did Joseph do when she grabbed his cloak?

skills.key_step: The child names trusted people (parent, teacher, church leader the child knows), says NO to strangers' offers and wrong requests, and knows whom to report to, including Childline Kenya 116.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the steps NO, GO, TELL.
floor.question: What are the three steps when someone asks you to do wrong?

representations: a circle of trusted people around the child
steps: Say NO to sweets or lifts from strangers.
Tell a trusted adult or call 116.
contexts: a stranger at the school gate
a lift offered on the way home
a phone call from an unknown number

board.do: Draw a child in the middle of a circle.
Point at the space outside the circle.
board.say: Is a stranger who offers sweets inside or outside your circle?

board.do: Wait for the child to say outside.
Write the names of trusted people inside the circle and 116 below.

misconceptions.ask: A stranger offers you sweets and a lift home. What should you do?
misconceptions.repair: Role-play a firm NO and walking to a shop, a teacher or a parent.

listen_for: Any adult who tells me to come
misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a trusted person for a child?
misconceptions.repair: List trusted people by name, and the rule that a trusted person never asks for a secret.

listen_for: No one, they will not believe me
misconceptions.ask: Whom can you report to if you are in danger?
misconceptions.repair: Say the list aloud and practise telling.

misconceptions.ask: Someone online knows your name and school and asks to meet. Is that a trusted person?
misconceptions.repair: Make two lists: people I know and trust at home, school and church; people who only know about me.

checks.question: A stranger offers you a lift. What do you do?
checks.answer: Say no, go away and tell a trusted adult

checks.question: Name one person a child can report to.
checks.answer: A parent (a teacher, the chief, Childline 116)

skills.key_step: The child says Psalm 125:1 compares those who trust in the Lord to Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken; trusting God means relying on him in trouble while still doing one's part.

floor.question: What did Jesus do when the storm came?

representations: a mountain drawn beside a figure
steps: Who is like Mount Zion? Those who trust the Lord.
A mountain is not moved by wind.
Trust God and still do your part.
contexts: Mount Kenya through wind and rain
a family in a hard season

board.do: Draw a mountain with wind lines blowing at it.

board.say: Who does the psalm say is like this mountain?

board.do: Wait for the child to say those who trust in the Lord.

misconceptions.ask: What does it mean to trust in the Lord, according to Psalm 125:1?
misconceptions.repair: Read Psalm 125:1 and ask what Mount Zion does when the wind blows.

listen_for: She does not study, she just prays
misconceptions.ask: Wanjiru trusts God to help her in an exam. What fits?
misconceptions.repair: Remind: the servants in the parable used what they had.

listen_for: Because they are strong in themselves
misconceptions.ask: Why can those who trust in the Lord not be shaken?
misconceptions.repair: Read Psalm 125:1-2 and ask who surrounds the people.

misconceptions.ask: In Psalm 125:1, who is like Mount Zion?
misconceptions.repair: Read the verse in two halves: "Those who trust in the Lord / are like Mount Zion". Ask what the first half is about.

checks.question: Who is like Mount Zion in Psalm 125:1?
checks.answer: Those who trust in the Lord

checks.question: Wanjiru trusts God about her exam. What should she also do?
